segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Welcome to Imagination Nights. [pause 3]

Lie down in a way that feels easy. Let the bed take all of your weight. [pause 8]

Breathe in slowly through your nose. And let it out through your mouth, a little longer than it went in. [pause 8]

Again. In. And a long, slow breath out. [pause 10]

Let your forehead go soft. Your jaw. Your shoulders. Your hands. [pause 10]

Now we will relax the body, one part at a time. You do not have to do anything. Just notice each part as I name it, and let it get heavy. [pause 8]

Your feet. Let them be warm and heavy. [pause 15]

Your calves and your knees. Heavy. [pause 15]

Your hips and your lower back. Let them sink. [pause 15]

Your belly. Let it rise and fall on its own. [pause 15]

Your chest. Your shoulders. Your arms, all the way down to your fingertips. [pause 15]

Your neck. Your face. The little muscles around your eyes. [pause 15]

Your whole body, heavy and warm, held by the bed. [pause 15]

There is nothing to do tonight but imagine. And imagining is something you already know how to do. [pause 8]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Tonight is for anyone working toward a finish line. A degree. A certificate. A book. A long project. Paying something off. Getting through a hard season. [pause 11]

When we are in the middle of something long, the end can feel unreal. We see only the next assignment, the next shift, the next payment. Tonight we step forward to the finish. [pause 13]

Picture the day it is done. Not the stress of the last week, but the moment you know it is over. Maybe you are holding a paper. Maybe you just close a laptop. Maybe someone hugs you. [pause 13]

Let yourself feel proud. Many of us are not used to that feeling. It is all right to practice it. [pause 13]

If you have started and stopped before, that is not a mark against you. Many people finish on the second or third try. Tonight you can picture this time as the time you get to the end. [pause 5]

This is imagination and feeling, not a promise of any result. Keep doing the work in the daytime. Tonight, rest with the end in view. [pause 18]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
It is the day it is finished. Notice where you are. A hall. An office. Your own kitchen table. [pause 27]

Feel what is in your hands. A diploma. The last page. The final receipt. [pause 30]

Notice the quiet in your chest where the pressure used to be. [pause 30]

Someone near you says, you did it. Hear the words. Let them land. [pause 30]

Think back for a moment to the hardest night of the whole thing. The one where you almost quit. [pause 30]

Now look at yourself today, on the other side of it. Let yourself be a little amazed. [pause 33]

Picture going home that evening. Taking off your shoes. Nothing due tomorrow. [pause 33]

Someone calls to congratulate you. You hear yourself say, thank you. I am really proud. [pause 33]

Before bed, you put the proof of it somewhere you will see it. On the fridge. On a shelf. [pause 35]

Say quietly, I finished. [pause 35]

Let that sentence be the last one in your mind tonight. [pause 37]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Now let the scene stay with you as you drift. [pause 10]

You do not have to hold it tightly. Just let it be there, warm and quiet, like a lamp left on in another room. [pause 15]

If your mind wanders, come back to one small detail. A sound. A word. A feeling in your hands. [pause 20]

This is only imagination, and imagination is allowed to be kind. [pause 20]

You might notice that your breathing is slower now than when we began. Let it stay slow. [pause 25]

Let your body grow heavier still. There is nowhere to go. [pause 25]

If you are still awake, that is fine. Lie quietly with the scene, and let the quiet do its work. [pause 30]

Rest now. [pause 60]
